text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to better understand the cause, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor).

Based on your history as a smoker with progressive right arm weakness, dropping objects, weight loss, and diabetes, I suspect a lung tumor in the upper lobe compressing the brachial plexus. I need to see a Chest_X-Ray and Chest_CTA to confirm the mass and its extent before we proceed with treatment.
